subject: Architecture
title: Egyptian Pyramid Construction
description: A fast breakdown of Egyptian Pyramid Construction for builders.

hook.text: The Great Pyramid weighs 6 million tons and was the tallest structure on Earth for 3,800 years.

buildup.text: 2.3 million limestone blocks, each weighing about 2.5 tons, were cut, moved, and stacked with precision.

discovery.text: Workers likely used water-lubricated ramps and sledges — wet sand reduces friction by 50%.

twist.text: Builders weren't slaves. Archaeological evidence shows they were paid workers who ate well and received medical care.

climax.text: The pyramid's base is level to within 2.1 centimeters across 756 feet — astonishing precision.

punchline.text: No wheels, no iron, no cranes. Just geometry, water, and determination.

quiz.question: How did workers reduce friction when moving pyramid blocks?
options: They rolled them on wooden logs
They used water-lubricated sand on sledge paths
They floated them on canals to the base

details.summary: Egyptian pyramids were built using millions of limestone blocks, each averaging 2.5 tons, moved by organized teams of skilled workers using ramps, sledges, and levers.
details.whyItMatters: The pyramids prove that ancient people achieved monumental feats through organization and ingenuity rather than lost technology. Understanding their construction dispels myths and reveals real engineering brilliance.
takeaways: Pyramids were built by organized skilled workers, not slaves
Ramps, sledges, and levers moved multi-ton limestone blocks

faq.question: How long did it take to build a pyramid?
faq.answer: The Great Pyramid at Giza took approximately 20 years with a workforce of 20,000-30,000 people. Workers quarried, transported, and placed roughly 2.3 million blocks. Seasonal labor during Nile floods provided the bulk of the workforce.

faq.question: Were the pyramids built by slaves?
faq.answer: No. Archaeological evidence shows the workers were paid laborers who received food, medical care, and housing. Worker cemeteries near Giza reveal respected burials. The workforce included skilled masons and seasonally rotated agricultural workers.
